_comment: ADR 0044/0045 — common physics body templates. Per-game entity defs spread these via $extends to get sensible defaults. Override individual fields after the $extends to customize. Bits 1..16 from @lib.physics.layers used here; games with custom layer names can override collision_layer / collision_mask. ADR 0045: `body_type: "character"` creates a CharacterBody3D Node (move_and_slide-driven, the right pick for velocity-controlled actors). Other body_types create raw PhysicsServer3D RIDs.

standard_character_player._comment: ADR 0045 — player CharacterBody3D. move_and_slide handles drag / collision / slope / floor; speed clamped to state.max_speed at 60Hz via character_body_runner. Use this for human-controlled actors (WASD-driven).

standard_character_npc._comment: ADR 0045 — NPC CharacterBody3D. Same body class as player but with NPC-shaped collision layer/mask. AI policies or schedule directors write state.velocity each tick; character_body_runner._physics_process consumes it.

standard_character_animal._comment: ADR 0045 — animal CharacterBody3D. Smaller capsule than NPC; mask excludes 'enemy' since most animals aren't hostile by default (override to add).

standard_kinematic_npc._comment: Legacy raw-RID kinematic body. Use for non-moving NPCs that only need to BLOCK motion (statues, props). Velocity-driven NPCs should use standard_character_npc instead — character bodies get Godot's move_and_slide for free.

standard_kinematic_animal._comment: Legacy raw-RID kinematic body. Use standard_character_animal for velocity-driven animals.

standard_kinematic_player._comment: Legacy raw-RID kinematic body. Use standard_character_player for WASD-controlled players (gives move_and_slide / slope / floor detection for free).

static_decoration_no_collision._comment: For visible-but-non-blocking decoration. No body = no physics overhead. Use this template by NOT declaring a physics block on the entity.

_authoring_note: Templates use $extends syntax: "physics": {"$extends": "@lib.physics.bodies.standard_kinematic_npc"}. Override individual fields by listing them after the $extends key — last-writer-wins per ADR 0027. Example: bigger wolf needs height: 1.0 → {"$extends": "@lib.physics.bodies.standard_kinematic_animal", "collision_shape": {"type": "capsule", "radius": 0.5, "height": 1.0}}.
